schema.title: Linkedin job scraper
schema.description:
ℹ️ This tool scrapes jobs from [public Linkedin jobs search page](https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/search) where available filters and  results can be different compared to search page on a logged in Linkedin account. To avoid confusion, generate search url by opening this url in an incognito window: https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/search 

 ℹ️ You can now use the AI search filters directly instead of URLs by leaving urls empty and providing at least one filter

 ℹ️ If you want to scrape jobs using logged in account then use [Advanced Linkedin jobs scraper](https://apify.com/curious_coder/linkedin-jobs-search-scraper). It also gives you more information like Apply URLs, Skills, Applicant insights, etc 

ℹ️ Related actors: [Indeed job scraper](https://apify.com/curious_coder/indeed-scraper)

urls.title: Linkedin jobs search URLs
urls.description:
Go to [public linkedin jobs search page](https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/search/) on incognito window (to access public version), search with required filters and once you are done, copy the full URL from address bar and pass it here. You can pass multiple search URLs.

When URLs are provided, the AI search filters below are ignored. Leave this empty to use the filters instead.

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Job title, skills, or free-text search (e.g. "software engineer remote"). Used only when the URLs list above is empty.
keywords.sectionDescription: Used only when no search URLs are provided. Only filters still supported by LinkedIn AI job search are listed here. Put experience, job type, workplace, salary, etc into Keywords if needed. [Click here](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a6889044) to learn more about AI jobs search.

location.title: Location
location.description: City, region, or country as you would type it on LinkedIn (e.g. "United States", "London, United Kingdom", "Remote").

geoId.title: Geo ID
geoId.description: Optional LinkedIn geoId for precise location targeting (found in a LinkedIn search URL as `geoId=`). Overrides free-text location when LinkedIn resolves it.

distance.title: Distance (miles)
distance.description: Search radius in miles around the location. Leave empty for LinkedIn's default.

datePosted.title: Date posted
datePosted.description: Only return jobs posted within this window.

companyIds.title: Company IDs
companyIds.description: LinkedIn numeric company IDs (from a company URL or `f_C=` in a search URL), e.g. "1441" for Google.

under10Applicants.title: Under 10 applicants
under10Applicants.description: Only jobs with fewer than 10 applicants.

autoConvertToAiSearch.title: Auto convert old search URLs to AI search URLs (recommended)
autoConvertToAiSearch.description:
LinkedIn is now forcing AI job search which removed many classic filters (experience, job type, workplace, salary, sort, etc.)

When this option is enabled, the filters in old search URLs are converted to natural language and appended to search keywords. Date posted, Company, Easy apply, and Under 10 applicants stay as URL filters on AI search.

scrapeCompany.title: Scrape company details
scrapeCompany.description: This will require additional scraping requests for each job record and take longer to scrape

limitPerSource.title: Max jobs per search
limitPerSource.description: Maximum number of jobs to scrape from each input URL (or from the AI search filters when no URLs are provided). Leave empty to scrape as many as LinkedIn returns for each search (up to ~1000).

splitByLocation.title: Split search by city locations
splitByLocation.description: Enable this to split your search by cities within a country. This helps bypass LinkedIn's 1000 job limit per search URL by creating separate searches for each city. This will overwrite the location filter in input search URLs.

splitCountry.title: Country to split by
splitCountry.description: Select the country whose cities will be used to split the search. Only used when 'Split search by city locations' is enabled. Required to when 'Split search by city locations' is enabled.

pricing.reasonForChange:
This price change only affects users on Apify free plan. Paying users are not affected. 

An additional negligible cost per actor start is added which is just $0.05 per 1000 actor starts.

apify-default-dataset-item.eventDescription: Single result in the default dataset.

apify-actor-start.eventDescription: Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).

position.title: Positions/keywords for search
position.description: Any combination of positions or keywords for search. Can be used together with Start URLs - both will be scraped independently, each limited by Max job listings per search.

maxItemsPerSearch.title: Max job listings per search
maxItemsPerSearch.description: Maximum number of job listings to scrape for each keyword search and each Start URL. When both are used together, each is limited independently by this value.

location.title: Location for search
location.description: Any combination of city, zip code or locality for search. Used together with position/keywords.

parseCompanyDetails.title: Scrape company details
parseCompanyDetails.description: If true, each job also includes company details: description, website URL, logo, company size and rating. These come from the same API response as the job itself, so turning this on costs no extra requests.

saveOnlyUniqueItems.title: Save only unique job listings
saveOnlyUniqueItems.description: If true, only unique job listings will be scraped.

followApplyRedirects.title: Follow redirects for apply link (no longer needed)
followApplyRedirects.description: Has no effect. `externalApplyLink` is now always the employer's own apply URL, because it comes resolved from Indeed's API instead of being followed by the scraper. Left in place so existing runs keep working.

startUrls.title: Start URLs
startUrls.description: List of URLs that will be scraped. Can be main website URL, category/search URLs, company jobs URL (in the format of `https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Google/jobs`) or detail/product URLs. Can be combined with keyword search - both will execute independently.
startUrls.sectionCaption: Also get results from custom URLs

result.eventDescription: Cost per every job listing returned.

schema.title: Google Search Results Scraper input
schema.description:
Use this to search Google the same way you normally would - for example, look for cute cats. Use a new line for each query. Click ▷ Start to begin the scrape. If you need guidance, follow this tutorial.

Note: usage and costs are calculated based on the number of pages scraped.

queries.title: Search term(s)
queries.description: Use regular search words or enter Google Search URLs. You can also apply [advanced Google search techniques](https://blog.apify.com/how-to-scrape-google-like-a-pro/), such as AI site:twitter.com or javascript OR python. You can also define selected search filters as separate fields below (in the Advanced search filters section). Just ensure that your queries do not exceed 32 words to comply with Google Search limits.
queries.prefill: What are the top 5 CRM tools
queries.example:
best SEO tools
apify web scraping

maxPagesPerQuery.title: Max pages per search
maxPagesPerQuery.description: Maximum number of pages to scrape per search query. Each page contains approximately 10 results.

aiOverview.title: ⏩ Add-on: Google AI Overview ($)
aiOverview.description: Get the complete AI Overview whenever Google shows one for your query - handy when the short snippet isn't enough. May take slightly longer than a standard run, and works best on queries likely to trigger an AI Overview. Costs extra per captured AI Overview - see the Pricing tab for your rate.

scrapeFullAiOverview.title: ⏩ Add-on: Google AI Overview ($)
scrapeFullAiOverview.description: Turn on to capture the full AI Overview whenever one appears.

aiOverview.sectionDescription:
Track how your brand shows up in AI answers, not just classic search results. Turn on the engines you care about and compare their responses side by side to do an AI visibility audit.

Available features:
  • Google AI Overviews
  • Google AI Mode
  • Gemini search
  • Perplexity AI search, including recency, related questions, and images
  • ChatGPT search
Pricing: you pay a small fee per successful result while these features are on, with bigger discounts on higher-tier plans. See the Pricing tab for your exact rate.

aiModeSearch.title: ⏩ Add-on: Google AI Mode ($)
aiModeSearch.description: See how your brand appears in Google AI Mode, Google's dedicated AI search interface on google.com (distinct from the AI Overview snippets in regular results). Great for AEO and GEO tracking. Costs extra per result - see the Pricing tab for your rate.

enableAiMode.title: ⏩ Add-on: Google AI Mode ($)
enableAiMode.description: Turn on to fetch Google AI Mode results for every query.

geminiSearch.title: ⏩ Add-on: Gemini search ($)
geminiSearch.description:
Get an AI answer from Google Gemini (gemini.google.com), Google's standalone assistant, separate from Google Search.

Costs extra per result - see the Pricing tab for your rate.

enableGemini.title: ⏩ Add-on: Gemini search ($)
enableGemini.description: Turn on to fetch a Gemini answer for every query.

perplexitySearch.title: ⏩ Add-on: Perplexity AI search ($)
perplexitySearch.description:
Get AI answers and citations from Perplexity's Sonar model.

Costs extra per result - see the Pricing tab for your rate.

enablePerplexity.title: ⏩ Add-on: Perplexity AI search ($)
enablePerplexity.description: Turn on to fetch a Perplexity answer for every query.

searchRecency.title: Search recency
searchRecency.description: Filter search results based on their recency.

returnImages.title: Include images in Perplexity AI answers
returnImages.description: Include relevant images in Perplexity's answer.

returnRelatedQuestions.title: Include related questions in Perplexity AI answers
returnRelatedQuestions.description: Include follow-up questions related to your query.

chatGptSearch.title: ⏩ Add-on: ChatGPT search ($)
chatGptSearch.description:
Get AI answers from OpenAI's search model.

Costs extra per result - see the Pricing tab for your rate.

enableChatGpt.title: ⏩ Add-on: ChatGPT search ($)
enableChatGpt.description: Turn on to fetch a ChatGPT answer for every query.

copilotSearch.title: ⏩ Add-on: Microsoft Copilot search ($)
copilotSearch.description: Get AI answers from Microsoft Copilot.

enableCopilot.title: ⏩ Add-on: Microsoft Copilot search ($)
enableCopilot.description: Turn on to fetch a Microsoft Copilot answer for every query.

copilotSearchMode.title: Microsoft Copilot search mode
copilotSearchMode.description:
Select which Microsoft Copilot chat mode to use for the request:

• chat - Standard conversational mode. Best for general queries and quick answers.
• reasoning - Deep analytical mode. Best for complex questions requiring logical depth.
• smart - Balanced mode combining speed and reasoning for most use cases.
• study - Detailed explanatory mode. Best for educational and research-oriented prompts.

maximumLeadsEnrichmentRecords.title: ⏩ Add-on: Extract business leads information: max leads per domain ($)
maximumLeadsEnrichmentRecords.description:
Maximum number of lead records to scrape per domain found. Set to 0 (the default) to disable leads enrichment.

⚠️ This returns personal data. You're responsible for having a legal basis to collect and use it under privacy laws.

⚠️ This value is a multiplier - see the section description above for how costs are calculated.
maximumLeadsEnrichmentRecords.sectionDescription:
Add contact and company details for the people behind each domain you find.

What you get: name, work email, phone number, job title, and LinkedIn profile, plus company data like industry and size.

Find the leads tied to each search result in the 'Organic results' tab.

⚠️ How costs work: the number you request is per domain found. Requesting 10 leads across 1,000 domains attempts 10,000 leads. You only pay for leads actually found. Higher-tier plans mean bigger discounts - see the Pricing tab for your exact rate.

Please be aware: enrichment runs on every domain in your results - news sites, directories, and comparison sites included, not just company websites.

leadsEnrichmentDepartments.title: Lead departments
leadsEnrichmentDepartments.description: Include only leads from specific departments, such as Sales, Marketing, or C-suite. Only applies when business leads enrichment (maximumLeadsEnrichmentRecords) is enabled. Note that some job titles may be miscategorized.

verifyLeadsEnrichmentEmails.title: ⏩ Add-on: Email verification ($)
verifyLeadsEnrichmentEmails.description:
Check whether each lead's email is actually deliverable before you reach out. Adds an emailVerification object to every lead with the result and a quality score.

Charged (decisive results): valid (ok), invalid, and disposable addresses.
Not charged: catch-all, unknown, and error results.

⚠️ Requires business leads enrichment to be enabled.

linkProspecting.title: 🔗 Add-on: Link prospecting tool ($)
linkProspecting.description:
Charged events: search-page-scraped (base, per Google SERP page), website-content-scraped, lead-scraped (up to 5 contacts per domain, marketing and C-suite roles only), and one event per enabled AI engine query. See the Pricing tab for rates.

⚠️ If business leads enrichment is also active, domains that appear in both organic results and AI citations may be enriched by both features and charged for leads separately.

⚠️ If the Full website content add-on is also active, pages shared between the two add-ons are scraped and charged only once.
linkProspecting.sectionDescription:
Find websites that cover your topic but don't yet mention your brand, then get outreach contacts for link building.

How it works: checks every URL cited in Google Search results, and any other AI engines enabled in the AI search visibility section above.

To enable: set Brand name below. Leave it empty to skip this add-on.

Where to find results: in a separate Link prospecting tool dataset.

brandName.title: Brand name
brandName.description: Your brand name to search for on every cited page. Setting this field enables the Link prospecting tool add-on. Pages where this name is found are saved with isBrandMentionedInSource: true. Pages where it is absent are saved with isBrandMentionedInSource: false and enriched with outreach contacts. Leave empty to disable this add-on.

ownDomains.title: Own domains
ownDomains.description: List of domains belonging to your brand. These are excluded from Link prospecting tool results - you don't need to find outreach contacts on your own site. Subdomains are also excluded when their root domain matches.

ignoredDomains.title: Ignored domains
ignoredDomains.description: List of domains to exclude from Link prospecting tool (e.g. competitor sites or well-known directories). Subdomains are also excluded when their root domain matches.

websiteContentScraper.title: 🔍 Add-on: Full website content ($)
websiteContentScraper.description:
Get the full page content of every organic result as websiteContent.text, plus websiteContent.markdown when the page converts cleanly (null otherwise). Uses the Website Content Crawler. Charged event: website-content-scraped, per successfully scraped page. See the Pricing tab for rates.

⚠️ If the Link prospecting tool add-on is also active, pages shared between the two add-ons are scraped and charged only once.

enable.title: 🔍 Add-on: Full website content ($)
enable.description: Turn on to scrape each organic result page and attach its content to the result item.

websiteContentScraper.sectionDescription: Pull the full page content behind your organic results so you can run content gap analysis, competitive audits, and SERP benchmarking.

focusOnPaidAds.title: 📢 Add-on: Paid results (ads) extraction ($)
focusOnPaidAds.description: Turn on to capture the Google Ads shown for each query.
focusOnPaidAds.sectionDescription:
Capture the Google Ads running for your keywords to benchmark competitor messaging and spot new campaigns.

How it works: uses an ad-specialized proxy with up to 3 retries per query to detect ads reliably. Best for queries likely to show ads, skip it for general scraping.

Pricing: costs extra per search page even if no ads are found. The value is in the complete check. See the Pricing tab for your rate.

countryCode.title: Country
countryCode.description: Country of the Google results, passed to Google Search as the gl URL query parameter. By default, the Actor uses United States. Google Search URLs are used as they are. The country is also sent to the LLM search engines. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and AI Mode do not support every country; if the selected one is not available, that engine returns no result.
enumTitles: Congo, the Democratic Republic of the
Macedonia, the Former Yugoslav Republic of
South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

searchLanguage.title: Search language
searchLanguage.description: Restricts search results to pages in a specific language. For example, choosing 'German' results in pages only in German. Passed to Google Search as the lr URL query parameter. Read more here.

languageCode.title: Interface language
languageCode.description: Language of the Google Search interface (menus, buttons, etc. - not the search results themselves). Passed to Google Search as the hl URL query parameter. It can still affect results on international queries when no search-language restriction (the lr parameter) is set. Read more here.

locationUule.title: Exact location (Google UULE parameter)
locationUule.description: The code for the exact location for the Google search. It's passed to Google Search as the uule URL query parameter. You can use the UULE code generator. Learn more about emulating local search.

forceExactMatch.title: Force exact match
forceExactMatch.description: If checked, the scraper will search for the exact phrase in the query. This is done by wrapping the query in quotes. Note that this may return fewer results. Also note that if you're using operators such as OR or AND, the whole query will be wrapped in quotes, such as "Windows AND macOS". If you want to search for queries such as "Windows" AND "macOS", you need to specify them directly in the queries field.
forceExactMatch.sectionDescription: Use these filters to narrow down your search results. You can use them in combination with your search terms above. Each filter will be applied to all queries except for the ones that already contain the given filter. For example, if you have a query literature site:example.com, the site filter will not be applied to it.

site.title: Site
site.description: Limits the search to a specific site, such as: site:example.com. Note that the site filter takes precedence over the relatedToSite filter. If both filters are set, the relatedToSite filter will be ignored and not added to the search queries.

relatedToSite.title: Related to site
relatedToSite.description: Filters pages related to a specific site, such as: related:example.com. Note that the site filter takes precedence over the relatedToSite filter. If both filters are set, the relatedToSite filter will be ignored and not added to the search queries.

wordsInTitle.title: Words in title
wordsInTitle.description: Filters pages with specific words in the title. The scraper uses the intitle: operator, even for multiple words (e.g. recipe site:allrecipes.com intitle:"easy apple" intitle:pie). There's also a allintitle: operator available, but it's problematic when combined with other search filters, so the scraper avoids using it. If you need to use the allintitle: operator specifically, you can include it in your custom queries from the queries field.

wordsInText.title: Words in text
wordsInText.description: Filters pages with specific words in the text. The scraper uses the intext: operator, even for multiple words (e.g. cartoon site:wikipedia.com intext:cat intext:mouse). There's also a allintext: operator available, but it's problematic when combined with other search filters, so the scraper avoids using it. If you need to use the allintext: operator specifically, you can include it in your custom queries from the queries field.

wordsInUrl.title: Words in URL
wordsInUrl.description: Filters pages with specific words in the URL. The scraper uses the inurl: operator, even for multiple words (e.g. recipe site:allrecipes.com inurl:apple inurl:pie). There's also a allinurl: operator available, but it's problematic when combined with other search filters, so the scraper avoids using it. If you need to use the allinurl: operator specifically, you can include it in your custom queries from the queries field.

quickDateRange.title: Quick date range
quickDateRange.description: Filters results from a specific date range. d[number] specifies the number of past days (e.g. the past 10 days can be written as d10). The same applies to hours, weeks, months, and years: h[number], w[number], m[number], y[number]. Example for the past year: 'y1' or even 'y'. The value is passed to Google Search using the tbs URL query parameter, prefixed with qdr:. You should avoid combining this filter with the beforeDate and afterDate filters to prevent conflicts.

beforeDate.title: Before date
beforeDate.description: Filters results from before the specified date. Either absolute date (e.g. `2024-05-03`) or relative date from now into the past (e.g. `8 days`, `3 months`). Absolute time is always interpreted in the UTC timezone, not your local timezone - please convert accordingly. Supported relative date & time units: `days`, `weeks`, `months`, `years`. You should avoid combining this filter with the `quickDateRange` filter to prevent conflicts.

afterDate.title: After date
afterDate.description: Filters results from after the specified date. Either absolute date (e.g. `2024-05-03`) or relative date from now into the past (e.g. `8 days`, `3 months`). Absolute time is always interpreted in the UTC timezone, not your local timezone - please convert accordingly. Supported relative date & time units: `days`, `weeks`, `months`, `years`. You should avoid combining this filter with the `quickDateRange` filter to prevent conflicts.

fileTypes.title: File types
fileTypes.description: Filters results of specific file types using the filetype: operator, such as filetype:pdf. You can select multiple file types as well. They will be combined with the OR operator, for example: filetype:doc OR filetype:txt. If you need to use a file type that is not in the list (such as a source code file type), you can include it in your custom queries from the queries field, using the filetype: operator.

mobileResults.title: Mobile results
mobileResults.description: If checked, the scraper returns results from the mobile version of Google Search. Otherwise, desktop results are returned.

includeUnfilteredResults.title: Unfiltered results
includeUnfilteredResults.description: If checked, the lower-quality results that Google normally filters out are included.

saveHtml.title: Save HTML to dataset
saveHtml.description: If checked, the HTML of the Google Search results pages is stored in the default dataset, under the html property. This is useful if you need to process the HTML, but it makes the dataset large.

saveHtmlToKeyValueStore.title: Save HTML to key-value store
saveHtmlToKeyValueStore.description: If checked, the HTML of the Google Search results pages is stored in the default key-value store, and links to the files are stored in the dataset under the htmlSnapshotUrl property. This is useful for debugging, since you can easily view the pages in the browser. Note that this feature may slow down the Actor.

includeIcons.title: Include icon image data (base64)
includeIcons.description: If checked, all of the results (organicResults, paidResults, suggestedResults) will contain Base64-encoded icon image data if found.

search-page-scraped.eventDescription: Cost per page of Google Search results successfully scraped.

ai-overview-scraped.eventDescription: Extra cost per query when an AI Overview is successfully captured. Uses a specialized proxy to increase the probability of getting one.

ai-mode-result-scraped.eventDescription: Extra cost for using Google AI Mode per search query. This cost is applied when a successful Google AI Mode request is returned.

perplexity-ai-result-scraped.eventDescription: Extra cost for using Perplexity AI search per search query. This cost is applied when a successful Perplexity AI search request is returned.

chatgpt-result-scraped.eventDescription: Extra cost for using ChatGPT search per search query. This cost is applied when a successful ChatGPT search request is returned.

copilot-result-scraped.eventDescription: Extra cost for using Copilot search per search query. This cost is applied when a successful Copilot search request is returned.

gemini-result-scraped.eventDescription: Extra cost for using Gemini search per search query. This cost is applied when a successful Gemini search request is returned.

lead-scraped.eventDescription: Cost per successfully extracted business lead. Get key prospect details: full name, work email, phone number, job title, and LinkedIn profile. Business leads are extracted based on the found web domains.

lead-email-verified.eventDescription: Cost per decisive email verification (valid, invalid, or disposable). You are not charged for catch-all, unknown, or error results.

ads-scraped.eventDescription: Extra cost per page for attempting to extract paid results (ads) from Google Search. This applies when the ads extraction feature is enabled, regardless of whether ads are found on the specific page.

website-content-scraped.eventDescription: Cost per website page successfully scraped.

apify-actor-start.eventDescription: Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).

schema.title: Input schema for Website Content Crawler
schema.description: Enter **Start URLs** of websites to crawl, ensure you are using the right **Crawler type**, check the other optional settings, and click **Start** to run the crawler.

startUrls.title: Start URLs
startUrls.description:
One or more URLs where the crawler will start. By default, it crawls only these URLs and their sub-pages (same URL path); use **Include URL patterns (globs)** to override this behavior.

For example, for start URL `https://example.com/blog`, it will crawl also `https://example.com/blog/post` or `https://example.com/blog/article`.

crawlerType.title: Crawler type
enumTitles: Adaptive switching between browser and raw HTTP. Recommended.
[DEPRECATED] Raw HTTP client with JavaScript (JSDOM) - This crawler will use Cheerio instead.
[DEPRECATED] Headless browser (Chrome+Playwright) - The crawler will use Firefox+Playwright instead.
crawlerType.description:
Select the crawling engine:
- **Adaptive switching** between browser and raw HTTP: Fast and renders JavaScript content if present. Default and recommended option.
- **Headless browser** (Firefox+Playwright): Reliable, renders JavaScript content, best in avoiding blocking, but might be slow.
- **Raw HTTP client** (Cheerio): Fastest, but doesn't render JavaScript content.
- **Raw HTTP client with JavaScript** (JSDOM): Deprecated, use Cheerio instead.
- **Headless browser** (Chrome+Playwright): Deprecated, use Firefox+Playwright instead.

More details about Crawler types are in [readme](https://console.apify.com/actors/aYG0l9s7dbB7j3gbS/information/version-0/readme#crawler-types).

includeUrlGlobs.sectionDescription: Configure which pages to crawl or skip, how deep to crawl, and how to discover more pages.
includeUrlGlobs.title: Include URL patterns (globs)
includeUrlGlobs.description:
Define URL patterns (globs) to extend crawling beyond **Start URLs** and their subpages.

Example: `https://www.example.com/blog/**` matches any blog page — `https://www.example.com/blog/post-title` or `https://www.example.com/blog/category/post` — even if the Start URL is `https://www.example.com/product/some-product`.

It affects only links found on pages, but not **Start URLs** - if you want to crawl a page, make sure to specify its URL in the **Start URLs** field.

Combined with **Exclude URL patterns**, you can precisely control which pages are crawled.

Learn more about globs [here](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tools/glob?comments=true&glob=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fscrape_this%2F%2A%2A&matches=false&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Ftools%2F&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fscrape_this%2F&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fscrape_this%2F123%3Ftest%3Dabc&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fdont_scrape_this) and test them with our **Glob tester** under this input.

excludeUrlGlobs.title: Exclude URL patterns (globs)
excludeUrlGlobs.description:
Glob patterns matching URLs of pages that will be excluded from crawling. Note that this affects only links found on pages, but not **Start URLs**, which are always crawled. 

For example `https://{store,docs}.example.com/**` excludes all URLs starting with `https://store.example.com/` or `https://docs.example.com/`, and `https://example.com/**/*\?*foo=*` excludes all URLs that contain `foo` query parameter with any value.

Learn more about globs [here](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tools/glob?comments=true&glob=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fscrape_this%2F%2A%2A&matches=false&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Ftools%2F&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fscrape_this%2F&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fscrape_this%2F123%3Ftest%3Dabc&tests=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fdont_scrape_this) and test them with our **Glob tester** under this input.

maxCrawlDepth.title: Max crawling depth
maxCrawlDepth.description:
The maximum number of links starting from the start URL that the crawler will recursively follow. The start URLs have depth `0`, the pages linked directly from the start URLs have depth `1`, and so on.

Useful to prevent accidental crawler runaway. By setting it to `0`, the Actor will only crawl the Start URLs.

maxCrawlPages.title: Max pages
maxCrawlPages.description:
The maximum number of pages to crawl: defaults to 9999999, which is effectively unlimited; set it to cap the number of pages to prevent accidental crawler runaway.

It includes the start URLs, pagination pages, pages with no content, etc. The crawler will automatically finish after reaching this number.

useSitemaps.title: Load URLs from Sitemaps
useSitemaps.description:
If enabled, the crawler will look for [Sitemaps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitemaps) at the domains of the provided *Start URLs* and enqueue matching URLs similarly as the links found on crawled pages.

You can also reference a `sitemap.xml` file directly by adding it as another Start URL (e.g. `https://www.example.com/sitemap.xml`)

The crawling could be more robust with Sitemaps, as it includes pages that might be not reachable from Start URLs. However, **loading and processing Sitemaps can take a lot of time, especially for large sites**.

Note that if a page is found via Sitemaps, it will have `depth` of `1`.

onlyCrawlPagesModifiedSince.title: Crawl only pages changed since (experimental)
onlyCrawlPagesModifiedSince.description:
If set, the crawler will only crawl URLs of pages that may have changed since the provided date. You can enter a date in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. On navigation, a page that returns a `304 Not Modified` response will be considered unchanged and skipped. **Start URL** is always crawled.

Works even better with `useSitemaps` enabled - a sitemap that contains `<lastmod>` tags will be used to determine if pages have changed and filter them out to save crawling resources. Pages without a `<lastmod>` tag will be enqueued regardless of this setting.

useLlmsTxt.title: Crawl /llms.txt and Markdown files
useLlmsTxt.description: If enabled, the crawler will look for `/llms.txt` files at the root of the domains of the provided Start URLs (e.g., `https://example.com/llms.txt`) and enqueue them for crawling. Note that this also enables crawling other Markdown files and enqueueing links from them.

respectRobotsTxtFile.title: Respect the robots.txt file
respectRobotsTxtFile.description: If enabled, the crawler will consult the robots.txt file for the target website before crawling each page. At the moment, the crawler does not use any specific user agent identifier. The crawl-delay directive is also not supported yet.

keepUrlFragments.title: URL #fragments identify unique pages
keepUrlFragments.description: Indicates that URL fragments (e.g. http://example.com#fragment) should be included when checking whether a URL has already been visited or not. Typically, URL fragments are used for page navigation only and therefore they should be ignored, as they don't identify separate pages. However, some single-page websites use URL fragments to display different pages; in such a case, this option should be enabled.

ignoreCanonicalUrl.title: Ignore canonical URLs
ignoreCanonicalUrl.description: If enabled, the Actor will ignore the canonical URL or the `ETag` header reported by the page, and use the actual URL instead. You can use this feature for websites that report invalid canonical URLs, which causes the Actor to skip those pages in results.

proxyConfiguration.sectionDescription: Customize location and identity settings of the crawler.
proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Enables loading the websites from IP addresses in specific geographies and to circumvent blocking.

initialCookies.title: Custom cookies
initialCookies.description:
Cookies that will be pre-set to all pages the scraper opens. This is useful for pages that require login. The value is expected to be a JSON array of objects with `name` and `value` properties. For example: 

```json
[
  {
    "name": "cookieName",
    "value": "cookieValue",
    "path": "/",
    "domain": ".apify.com"
  }
]
```

You can use the [EditThisCookie](https://docs.apify.com/academy/tools/edit-this-cookie) browser extension to copy browser cookies in this format, and paste it here.

Note that the value is secret and encrypted to protect your login cookies.

customHttpHeaders.title: Custom HTTP headers
customHttpHeaders.description: HTTP headers that will be added to all requests made by the crawler. This is useful for setting custom authentication headers or other headers required by the target website. The value is expected to be a JSON object with `name` and `value` properties pairs. For example: `{ "name1": "value1", "Authorization": "Basic a1b2c3d4..." }`.

signHttpRequests.title: Sign HTTP requests (experimental)
signHttpRequests.description: If enabled, the crawler will sign all HTTP requests using its Web Bot Auth private key. This is necessary if you want to use Website Content Crawler as a Cloudflare Signed Agent.

initialConcurrency.sectionDescription: Adjust how fast or slow the crawler will operate.
initialConcurrency.title: Initial concurrency
initialConcurrency.description:
The initial number of web browsers or HTTP clients running in parallel. The system scales the concurrency up and down based on the current CPU and memory load. If the value is set to 0 (default), the Actor uses the default setting for the specific crawler type.

Note that if you set this value too high, the Actor will run out of memory and crash. If too low, it will be slow at start before it scales the concurrency up.

maxConcurrency.title: Max concurrency
maxConcurrency.description: The maximum number of web browsers or HTTP clients running in parallel. This setting is useful to avoid overloading the target websites and to avoid getting blocked.

requestTimeoutSecs.title: Page request timeout
requestTimeoutSecs.description: Timeout in seconds for making the request and processing its response. Defaults to 60s.

minFileDownloadSpeedKBps.title: Minimum file download speed
minFileDownloadSpeedKBps.description: The minimum viable file download speed in kilobytes per seconds. If the file download speed is lower than this value for a prolonged duration, the crawler will consider the file download as failing, abort it, and retry it again (up to "Maximum number of retries" times). This is useful to avoid your crawls being stuck on slow file downloads.

maxRequestRetries.title: Maximum number of retries on network / server errors
maxRequestRetries.description: The maximum number of times the crawler will retry the request on network, proxy or server errors. If the (n+1)-th request still fails, the crawler will mark this request as failed.

maxSessionRotations.title: Maximum number of session rotations
maxSessionRotations.description: The maximum number of times the crawler will rotate the session (IP address + browser configuration) on anti-scraping measures like CAPTCHAs. If the crawler rotates the session more than this number and the page is still blocked, it will finish with an error.

ignoreHttpsErrors.title: Ignore HTTPS errors
ignoreHttpsErrors.description: If enabled, the scraper will ignore HTTPS certificate errors. Use at your own risk.

dynamicContentWaitSecs.sectionDescription: Simulate user interactions, fetch dynamic or hidden content.
dynamicContentWaitSecs.title: Wait for dynamic content
dynamicContentWaitSecs.description:
The maximum time in seconds to wait for dynamic page content to load. By default, it is 10 seconds. The crawler will continue processing the page either if this time elapses, or if it detects the network became idle as there are no more requests for additional resources.

When using the **Wait for selector** option, the crawler will wait for the selector to appear for this amount of time. If the selector doesn't appear within this period, the request will fail and will be retried.

Note that this setting is ignored for the raw HTTP client, because it doesn't execute JavaScript or loads any dynamic resources. Similarly, if the value is set to `0`, the crawler doesn't wait for any dynamic to load and processes the HTML as provided on load.

waitForSelector.title: Wait for selector
waitForSelector.description:
Specify a **CSS selector** to tell the crawler to wait for a specific element to appear before it starts extracting content. This is helpful for pages where the content loads dynamically.

Examples: `div`, `#id-of-an-element`, `.class-name`

This setting disables the default content-load detection. If the element doesn't appear within the **Wait for dynamic content** timeout, the request will fail and be retried.

If **Wait for dynamic content** is set to `0`, the crawler does not wait for late elements. Instead, it checks the selector only against the current page state / HTML snapshot, and fails the request immediately if the selector is not found.

With the raw HTTP client, this option checks for the presence of the selector in the HTML content and throws an error if it's not found.

softWaitForSelector.title: Soft wait for selector
softWaitForSelector.description: If set, the crawler will wait for the specified CSS selector to appear in the page before proceeding with the content extraction. Unlike the `waitForSelector` option, this option doesn't fail the request if the selector doesn't appear within the timeout (the request processing will continue).

maxScrollHeightPixels.title: Maximum scroll height
maxScrollHeightPixels.description:
The crawler will scroll down the page until all content is loaded (and network becomes idle), or until this maximum scrolling height is reached. Setting this value to `0` disables scrolling altogether.

Note that this setting is ignored for the raw HTTP client, because it doesn't execute JavaScript or loads any dynamic resources.

removeCookieWarnings.title: Remove cookie warnings
removeCookieWarnings.description:
If enabled, the Actor will try to remove cookies consent dialogs or modals, using the [I don't care about cookies](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/i-dont-care-about-cookies/) browser extension, to improve the accuracy of the extracted text. Note that there is a small performance penalty if this feature is enabled.

This setting is ignored when using the raw HTTP crawler type.

blockMedia.title: Block loading of images and videos
blockMedia.description: If the flag is enabled and the Actor is using a headless browser, it will not load images, fonts, stylesheets and videos to improve performance. It will load scripts as usual - that is after all the point of using a headless browser.

expandIframes.title: Expand iframe elements
expandIframes.description: By default, the Actor will extract content from `iframe` elements. If you want to specifically skip `iframe` processing, disable this option. Works only for the `playwright:firefox` crawler type.

clickElementsCssSelector.title: Expand clickable elements
clickElementsCssSelector.description: A CSS selector matching DOM elements that will be clicked. This is useful for expanding collapsed sections, in order to capture their text content. The value must be a valid CSS selector as accepted by the `document.querySelectorAll()` function.

stickyContainerCssSelector.title: Make containers sticky
stickyContainerCssSelector.description: This is an **experimental** feature. A CSS selector matching DOM elements that will be prevented from deleting any of their children. This is useful in conjunction with the "Expand clickable elements" option on pages where hidden content is actually removed from the DOM (i.e., some variants of the accordion pattern). Enabling this might corrupt the extracted content, which is why it is disabled by default. It is possible to enable the feature for the whole page with the `*` selector, or you can target specific elements if the former has unwanted side effects.

pageFunction.title: Page function
pageFunction.description:
A declaration of an asynchronous JS function (e.g. `async function pageFunction({ page }) { await page.click('.submit-button') }`).

The function receives `context` as the only argument. Context is a JavaScript object containing the following properties:
- `page`: Currently loaded Playwright `Page` instance.
- `request`: The request object that triggered the page load.

The function will be executed in the browser context for each crawled page, after the page is loaded (included all dynamic content) and before the content is extracted and cleaned.

keepElementsCssSelector.sectionDescription: Set which HTML elements to scrape or ignore. By default, the crawler removes common clutter, but here you can fine-tune the settings.
keepElementsCssSelector.title: Keep HTML elements (CSS selector)
keepElementsCssSelector.description:
Extract only relevant page content by specifying CSS selectors (e.g. `div`, `#element-id`, `.class-name`). [Learn more about CSS selectors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Styling_basics/Basic_selectors).

If any selectors are defined, everything else will be removed from the page.

This option runs before the `HTML transformer` option. If you are missing content in the output despite using this option, try disabling the `HTML transformer`.

removeElementsCssSelector.title: Remove HTML elements (CSS selector)
removeElementsCssSelector.description:
Specify which HTML elements should be removed from the page before text extraction. This is useful to skip irrelevant page content.

By default, the Actor removes common navigation elements, headers, footers, modals, scripts, and inline image. You can disable the removal by setting this value to some non-existent CSS selector like `dummy_keep_everything`.
removeElementsCssSelector.default:
nav, footer, script, style, noscript, svg, img[src^='data:'],
[role="alert"],
[role="banner"],
[role="dialog"],
[role="alertdialog"],
[role="region"][aria-label*="skip" i],
[aria-modal="true"]
removeElementsCssSelector.prefill:
nav, footer, script, style, noscript, svg, img[src^='data:'],
[role="alert"],
[role="banner"],
[role="dialog"],
[role="alertdialog"],
[role="region"][aria-label*="skip" i],
[aria-modal="true"]

htmlTransformer.title: HTML transformer
htmlTransformer.description:
Specify how to transform HTML to get meaningful content, removing extra fluff like navigation or pop-ups. This is applied after any HTML elements are removed or clicked.

- **Readable text with fallback**: Uses Mozilla's Readability to extract content, but keeps the original HTML if it's not a clear article. Great for sites with mixed content like articles and product pages.

- **Readable text** (Default): Also uses Mozilla's Readability but is more aggressive, removing headers, footers, and navigation. Best for blogs and article-heavy sites.

- **Extractus**: An alternative content extraction algorithm that might work better for certain news sites or blogs with unique layouts.

- **Defuddle**: More forgiving than Readability, better preserving elements like math and footnotes, code. It also extracts metadata and uses mobile styles for clean-up.

- **None**: Only performs basic cleaning and removes elements specified by you. This option is best when you need to preserve most of the page's original HTML.

readableTextCharThreshold.title: Readable text extractor character threshold
readableTextCharThreshold.description: A configuration options for the "Readable text" HTML transformer. It contains the minimum number of characters an article must have in order to be considered relevant.

aggressivePrune.title: Remove duplicate text lines
aggressivePrune.description: This is an **experimental feature**. If enabled, the crawler will prune content lines that are very similar to the ones already crawled on other pages, using the Count-Min Sketch algorithm. This is useful to strip repeating content in the scraped data like menus, headers, footers, etc. In some (not very likely) cases, it might remove relevant content from some pages.

debugMode.title: Debug mode (stores output of all HTML transformers)
debugMode.description: If enabled, the Actor will store the output of all types of HTML transformers, including the ones that are not used by default, and it will also store the HTML to Key-value Store with a link. All this data is stored under the `debug` field in the resulting Dataset.

debugLog.title: Debug log
debugLog.description: If enabled, the actor log will include debug messages. Beware that this can be quite verbose.

storeSkippedUrls.title: Store skipped URLs
storeSkippedUrls.description: If enabled, the crawler will store all URLs that were skipped during the crawl in a Key-Value Store record named `SKIPPED_URLS`. The record will contain a JSON object with reasons for skipping and the URLs that were skipped for each reason. This is useful for debugging and understanding why certain pages were not crawled.

saveHtml.title: Save HTML to dataset (deprecated)
saveHtml.description: If enabled, the crawler stores full transformed HTML of all pages found to the output dataset under the `html` field. **This option has been deprecated** in favor of the `saveHtmlAsFile` option, because the dataset records have a size of approximately 10MB and it's harder to review the HTML for debugging.

saveHtmlAsFile.title: Save HTML to key-value store
saveHtmlAsFile.description: If enabled, the crawler stores full transformed HTML of all pages found to the default key-value store and saves links to the files as `htmlUrl` field in the output dataset. Storing HTML in key-value store is preferred to storing it into the dataset with the `saveHtml` option, because there's no size limit and it's easier for debugging as you can easily view the HTML.

saveMarkdown.title: Save Markdown
saveMarkdown.description: If enabled, the crawler converts the transformed HTML of all pages found to Markdown, and stores it under the `markdown` field in the output dataset.

summarize.title: Summarize pages with AI (experimental) ($)
summarize.description:
If enabled, the crawler generates a one-sentence AI summary of each crawled web page and stores it under the `summary` field in the output dataset. This helps downstream LLM processing by describing what each page is about without reading the full content. Only web pages that have headings or extracted Markdown are summarized (files such as PDFs or images are not).

**This is a paid feature.** Summaries are generated through the OpenRouter Actor, which starts additional Actor runs and incurs extra cost on top of the crawl (billed to your account).

saveFiles.title: Save files
saveFiles.description: Deprecated in favor of the `saveContentTypes` option. Will be removed soon. If enabled, the crawler downloads files linked from the web pages, as long as their URL has one of the following file extensions: PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, and CSV. Note that unlike web pages, the files are downloaded regardless if they are under **Start URLs** or not. The files are stored to the default key-value store, and metadata about them to the output dataset, similarly as for web pages.

saveContentTypes.title: Save linked files with Content-Type
saveContentTypes.description: The crawler downloads files linked from the web pages, as long as their content type matches the provided value. Select predefined Content-type groups to download common file types, or enter custom HTTP Content-type strings, including wildcards (e.g., application/pdf, text/\*, image/\*) for specific downloads. Note that unlike web pages, the files are downloaded regardless if they are under **Start URLs** or not. The files are stored to the default key-value store, and metadata about them to the output dataset, similarly as for web pages.

saveScreenshots.title: Save screenshots (headless browser only)
saveScreenshots.description:
If enabled, the crawler stores a screenshot for each article page to the default key-value store. The link to the screenshot is stored under the `screenshotUrl` field in the output dataset. It is useful for debugging, but reduces performance and increases storage costs.

Note that this feature only works with the `playwright:firefox` crawler type.

maxResults.title: Max results
maxResults.description: The maximum number of web pages and files to store. This setting helps prevent an accidental crawler runaway by automatically stopping the crawl once this limit is reached. Note that the crawler skips pages whose canonical URL matches a page that has already been crawled, so it may crawl more pages than the number of stored results. Similarly, there may be more stored results than crawled web pages because downloaded files also count toward results.

clientSideMinChangePercentage.title: (Adaptive crawling only) Minimum client-side content change percentage
clientSideMinChangePercentage.description: The least amount of content (as a percentage) change after the initial load required to consider the pages client-side rendered

renderingTypeDetectionPercentage.title: (Adaptive crawling only) How often should the crawler attempt to detect page rendering type
renderingTypeDetectionPercentage.description: How often should the adaptive attempt to detect page rendering type

reuseStoredDetectionResults.title: Reuse stored detections results (experimental)
reuseStoredDetectionResults.description: If enabled, the crawler (if using playwright:adaptive) will reuse results of rendering type detections done in previous runs to speed up crawling of statically rendered pages
